description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise registered supported_operation_bundles and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>.v1. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare http_compatibility_bindings or unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. kind=branched declares a semantic request discriminator plus a closed effect_branches[] list with unique equals values and one final otherwise branch; each branch contains a complete event_log, actor_private_event, or none leaf effect. An event_log branch that is not unconditional MUST additionally name event_submission_path pointing to the caller-signed EventInitialSubmission used by that branch. Field presence is evidence carried by a branch, never the branch discriminator itself. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

Every operation_id is an explicit versioned operation identity ending in .v1. Its stable HTTP endpoint identity is derived by removing the terminal .vN and is used as the OpenAPI operationId; the unversioned identity is not an alias for a versioned operation_id.

Every canonical Arkret HTTP request MUST carry exactly one Arkret-Operation header naming the exact versioned operation_id before body parsing. The receiver MUST verify that the selector is locally advertised and belongs to the selected method/path family and binding. A missing selector fails with operation_selector_required; an empty candidate set, unknown id, duplicate selector, or value outside the route family fails with unsupported_operation_version. Endpoint uniqueness, payload-shape inference, client SDK version, implicit defaults, and version fallback MUST NOT replace the selector. This invariant keeps existing clients stable when another operation version is added to the same HTTP endpoint family.

operation_bundles is the only canonical bundle member source. Each registered bundle freezes one service_kind and a canonical unique set of (operation_id,binding_kind) members; changing a member requires a new bundle id.
Within one service_kind, active current-v1 bundles MUST NOT overlap on an identical (operation_id,binding_kind) pair. Pairs using a different binding kind are distinct.

Only registered ak.operation_bundle.*.v1 ids may appear in current-v1 ServiceDescribe. Current-v1 defines no vendor bundle wire namespace; vendor-private collections may only appear as ignorable x_* metadata and never affect capability decisions. Unknown bundle ids fail closed and are never expanded by name.

Request wire/canonical byte budget violations MUST return payload_too_large (HTTP 413); count-only schema violations with valid request bytes MUST return schema_violation (HTTP 422), except explicit operation count semantics. An otherwise valid request whose complete response or evaluation exceeds its semantic budget returns limit_exceeded (HTTP 413) or its defined typed unavailable result. Request byte errors take precedence over coincident schema errors. Error classification MUST NOT depend on diagnostic text substring matching.

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

delivery_authentication_record.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method and key digest; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id; registration_epoch is the effective destination Applet registration.
delivery_authentication_record.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare did MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. The effective registration_epoch and actual verification key digest are bound. Direct DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.
delivery_authentication_record.equality: Receivers recompute sha256(UTF8(digest_domain + newline) || RFC8785_JCS(record)); equal recomputed digests define replay equality. Caller-supplied records or digests are forbidden.

operations.notes: All directions preserve the unique original producer proof and portable signer authorization. Each receiver verifies exact installation aggregate, scope, grant, epoch and native act-on-behalf authority independently. HTTP source signatures and storage receipts do not authorize Events. Signals retain their independent proof regime.

The Applet service consumes the one signed install_bot or provision_ghost authoring request and returns the exact role-neutral four-Event bundle. Its durable ledger is keyed by branch subject plus full signed-request digest and preserves exact request/bundle bytes, actor key handle, method history, and provision state. No derived request ID or branch-specific Event aliases exist.

durable_effect.rationale: The operation admits no Arkret Event; independently, the Applet service atomically persists the subject/request-digest ledger, exact request and bundle, actor key custody, method history, and provision state before returning

did_authority.purpose: Verify the announce governance proof of the announcing service or organization, and resolve the Station endpoint inside the same first-ingest admission.
Verify the withdraw governance signature of the service or organization that owns the directory entry.

operations.notes: Consume an identity-abandonment challenge and explicitly abandon the provisional identity. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the presented handoff MUST be a fresh one and MUST NOT be the grant that was presented when the challenge was issued. Whether that fresh handoff required re-authentication, which risk checks ran and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified. One transaction consumes the challenge, records the orphan anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppresses the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releases the identity-creation lease; any step failing means zero writes. If the PCR was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because removing an established identity is the account deletion path. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 stays a permanently unusable orphan anchor; its later handling is deployment governance.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Station validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether the issuer ledger considers it active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/cell. Introspection does not call back to the origin Station and carries no reusable revocation-gate receipt: before accepting each protected self request, that origin Station checks its own exact device/generation pending/Seal state locally in the request transaction. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Station can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority S2S producer operation for Agent signer evidence. The request carries agent_authority_resolution: the service identity/type, adapter-discriminated method evidence and authenticated normalized DID Document. The receiver independently validates method evidence, document digest, current method state, project(did), and active assertion key before verifying an RFC 9421 signature that covers method, target URI/path, Content-Digest, Source/Destination-Service-ID, operation id and request id. A did_core_id, URL, bearer or caller-supplied public key is never the verification key source; bearer may only be an additional deployment gate. The authenticated source service MUST equal request.agent_authority_id and MUST byte-match service_id in request.principal_id's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding; that Station is the Agent PCR authority under the Agent same-server invariant. Ordinary clients and a caller-supplied account identity are forbidden. The Account Authority reads its own authoritative account binding/status projection, selects account_binding_default or account_status_event basis, and signs the closed controller_account_gate_attestation under domain ak.controller_account_gate.v1. issued_at <= expires_at and expires_at-issued_at MUST be <=300s. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable not_found outcomes and disclose no account status. Exact request_id plus canonical intent replay returns the byte-identical outcome while retained; same request_id with different principal or service is duplicate_conflict with zero issuance. The attestation is intentionally a reusable short-TTL controller-lifecycle snapshot and omits operation, request_digest, audience and challenge: the independently signed gate binds the controller principal and is reusable for the same applicable relationship. Actual operation, scope and possession are checked from each signed message; no additional observation or outer attestation exists. account_id and raw account cells never enter the request, outcome, logs visible to the caller or portable evidence.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus did rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve did itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(did)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Station co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, did, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Issue a single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.2). Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header, and by nothing else: the PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and therefore no principal-bound ak.session.grant. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, requires principal_id and did_version_id to equal the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that PCR is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id, did_version_id, lease id and fence, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from ordinary login, session resume, lease fence advance or any automated flow.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantIntent; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled. If deployment policy permits reactivation and the original account is deactivated, this operation alone atomically authors the deactivated-to-active successor, restores the same account row, creates the publication outbox entry and issues the first new-generation grant. It never creates a replacement account or second PCR, and it never revives an old session, device or KeyPackage; policy denial or incomplete recovery returns account_deactivated with zero authoritative writes.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger SessionGrant issuance with a closed HumanSessionGrantRequest | RecoverySessionGrantRequest | AgentSessionGrantRequest union. OIDC authorization code is never accepted here; authentication-handoffs is the unique code consumer. Returning-human and recovery requests use Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP. Returning-human issuance requires AcceptedDevicePossessionProof and origin revocation-gate allow, consumes the handoff, and emits Standard + complete device_binding. Recovery issuance requires credential_class=recovery_session, binds the account principal/audience, candidate device and handoff DPoP JWK, emits a <=15 minute non-refreshable recovery_candidate_device grant without device_binding, consumes only the request DPoP JTI, and preserves the handoff for recovery completion. Agent issuance keeps its independent agent_key_proof validator. The issuer uses branch-specific request identity and canonical intent to persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. Exact replay is byte-identical; conflict and terminal replay fail closed. The client presents every grant only as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP proof. No Principal Event is authored.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The handler validates the ak.session.grant + DPoP when metadata remains, idempotently terminates the Auth-side auth session / complete grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session.v1 when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Exact retries on an already terminal or pruned chain return an equivalent successful no-op; audience mismatch still fails closed. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1 request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's complete grant rotation chain. Exact retries, including an already logged-out, revoked, unknown or pruned chain, return an equivalent successful terminal outcome without a second side effect. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

One controller-signed authorize Event with inline Ed25519 public_key, exact supersedes and private scope disclosure binds a frozen candidate by pairing_request_id and approval_request_id. The verifier reads its authoritative frozen record (or authenticated verifier-only agent view), independently verifies PoP and candidate, and persists the exact command. Same-candidate PoP refresh does not invalidate approval. Accepted Seal processing automatically activates after rechecking current handle, expiry, candidate, parent authority and activation fence; cancellation or changed authority is terminal. Exact retry returns/reconciles the durable outcome and never revives authority.

Durable terminal exact replay is keyed by pairing request id, approving AccountId/device and canonical request digest. It returns the same accepted result without a second Event or stage consumption; same identity with changed intent conflicts.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger SessionGrant rotation with a closed HumanSessionGrantRefreshRequest | AgentSessionGrantRefreshRequest union. Both branches present the predecessor as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof and carry no client-generated challenge or generic proof_kind. Human refresh additionally carries AcceptedDevicePossessionProof purpose=session_grant_refresh; the origin verifies it under the locked current accepted-device key and applies the predecessor signed device_binding as expected binding in the same current-authorization linearization. Agent refresh carries only AgentSessionRefreshProof and revalidates current runtime-key authorization/lifecycle through its independent validator. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves subject/scope/audience/cnf.jkt/session_id, and atomically supersedes the predecessor. Exact replay returns the recorded successor; conflicting or terminal replay never issues another. Account/passkey restoration uses a fresh AccountHandoff then issue, and PCR recovery uses its dedicated completion operation; neither is a refresh proof kind. No Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer did and principal_id; every repeated did/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified did, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: The only client entry point for self-initiated account erasure (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface: it authenticates the holder as a high-risk action, durably records the erasure intent and continues its existing erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord issuance flow within the same service — there is no cross-service handoff, because the record issuer, the status-transition legality oracle and the section-8 fanout orchestrator are all the Account Authority, so no 'accepted but issuance pending on another service' intermediate state exists. Authentication freshness is judged locally by the Account Authority, the only party holding recent login / WebAuthn / recovery key facts; a Station MUST NOT determine or approximate it from session-grant introspection or local session state (introspection deliberately projects neither auth_time nor proof kind). The success response is an acceptance confirmation only: the current status is observed through the existing account-status read surface and physical completion only through the erasure receipt rail. The Account Authority MAY insert a deployment-governed withdrawal window (possibly zero) between acceptance and record signing, echoing withdrawal_window_ends_at when one exists; once the erasure_pending record is signed the request is irreversible and any withdrawal MUST fail closed. Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded acceptance outcome; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes; a different request_id while a live unsigned-record intent exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending. A session that does not satisfy the deployment's fresh high-risk action authentication policy is rejected with reauthentication_required.

Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Unique current-v1 OIDC authorization-code consumer. Account Authority exchanges and validates the code and issues an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key plus the deployment-local stable account_subject. The external callback receiver that owns the redirect transaction validates state; Account Authority validates state only when it owns that transaction, and always validates issuer, token exchange/PKCE, redirect_uri and ID Token nonce. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy. Bound clients normalize local evidence before choosing returning issue, pairing-first Device Setup or diagnostics; identity onboarding accepts only the other two states. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. When deployment policy allows reactivation, fresh account authentication may return a bound recovery-candidate handoff for the original deactivated account, but the handoff does not change status and ordinary register, issue and refresh remain blocked; only recovery completion may reactivate it. Policy denial returns account_deactivated with zero recovery writes.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime submits one candidate with an Ed25519 PoP over the authoritative handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, service DID, stable raw-key binding and at-most-five-minute window. Same-binding retries refresh the verified PoP while preserving candidate/approval/notification identity; different candidate on one handle conflicts. Controller signs the inline-key authorize Event once; approval is independent of PoP refresh. Secret and proof occur only in request body and confidential verifier material.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries the authorized key binding plus current_signer_evidence and signer_resolution_evidence_ref. The runtime compares authorized_public_key_digest against its own key, independently verifies and rebuilds the signer evidence/ref, persists that closure, and then authors ordinary Events offline; authorized_event_ref never substitutes for signer_resolution_evidence_ref. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the current public principal resolution projection from the known Station. The response carries only the account pair, the projection, bounded adapter method evidence and the Station projection attestation; it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted Seal. Account-internal audit material moved to ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1, so this surface has no history selector. This is a second-hop projection fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, verify the attestation proof under the current station_id method history, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(did)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventInitialSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

discriminator.description: The caller-declared semantic MIMI update kind. The decoded opaque payload MUST carry the same kind before a branch is admitted.

operations.notes: Returns current AuthenticatedServiceResolution containing service_id, service_kind, complete method_history_evidence and normalized_did_document. Consumers independently verify method-native history, current state, service identity/type, unique canonical HTTPS DID service endpoint and second-hop describe binding. Durable native method state prevents rollback and fork; cache TTL is at most 300 seconds and failed freshness checks never extend it. Endpoint refresh does not require Realm rebind; a changed service core requires a new authorized binding.

Back-binding activation of one provisioned private record to exactly one accepted ak.invite.third_party (third-party-invites.md section 7.5). The body carries provisioning_id and the Station-signed ThirdPartyInviteAcceptanceAttestation; the attestation is the whole authorization, so a caller-reported invite id, a caller-computed invite digest, an Event signature or an HTTP success MUST NOT be accepted in its place. The service verifies the Station service identity and signature, audience, exact verification_id, the attestation's signed expires_at/invite_expires_at bounds, and member-for-member equality of author, Realm, expiry and public material against the frozen provisioning record, recomputes invite_digest from the attested cell per section 4.2, then atomically persists the unique binding and the delivery intent. One provisioning record binds to one invite forever: a second attestation naming a different invite, Realm or author is refused and never rebinds, rotates the key or reissues the token. A byte-identical retry, a concurrent duplicate and a retry after a restart all return the original binding.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Delivery to an external mail or SMS gateway cannot be recalled. The intent MUST be durable before success is returned, and the delivered material stays the one invite this activation bound; stopping an already delivered invite requires an authorized writer's ak.invite.revoke.

operations.notes: Token presentation surface of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 4.1). The invitee's client submits invite_token, realm_id, subject_account_id, subject_did and a client claim_nonce in the JSON body; the service validates token, expiry, claim count and Realm binding, atomically consumes the token, signs the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript with the invite's verification_public_key and returns invite_id, token_commitment and binding_proof. invite_token in the URL query string or path segment is rejected with third_party_invite_token_in_query and the token SHOULD be invalidated; a knock_restricted Realm is rejected with unsupported_join_rule; every other failure is non-enumerable (section 6). A consumed token MUST NOT be re-bound to a different subject; the same (realm_id, subject_account_id, claim_nonce) MAY be answered with the same binding_proof inside the recoverable window (section 6.1).

Private-material provisioning entry of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 7.2). An authenticated inviter submits request_id, realm_id, inviter_account_id, verification_id, oob_code_kind, the private mailto:/tel: delivery target and the requested expiry, signed under ak.third_party_invite_provision_request_proof.v1 with the service DID as audience. The service mints and durably keeps the token, the per-invite 256-bit token_salt or lookup pepper and the per-invite ephemeral signing key, then returns only the public third_party_invite object, the effective expires_at, the activation deadline and an opaque provisioning_id. It MUST NOT return the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key or the delivery target, MUST NOT create a pending Realm Invite, MUST NOT mint an invite_id and MUST NOT deliver anything before activation. Same request_id plus byte-identical canonical intent replays the original outcome; same request_id plus different intent is duplicate_conflict with no second set of material. An unimplemented oob_code_kind or delivery scheme is unsupported_feature; every existence failure stays non-enumerable (section 6).

Lifecycle and out-of-band delivery position of one provisioning record (third-party-invites.md section 7.6). provisioning_id is the whole query credential and MUST travel only in the JSON body. It is the recovery surface after a lost provisioning or activation response and the only standard delivery observation point. The outcome carries provisioning_state, and once activated also invite_id, activated_at, delivery_state and delivery_attempt_count; it MUST NOT carry the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key, delivery target or any 3PID-derived value, and MUST NOT reveal whether the invitee opened the invite. An unknown handle, a handle belonging to another inviter and a deleted record MUST be indistinguishable.

Replicates one exact Account Authority-signed AccountStatusRecord. The receiver verifies transport authentication, record identity/proof, exact account/principal/binding tuple, sequence continuity and previous_account_status_record_id, then atomically advances its monotonic replica and emits a signed receipt. A gap returns dependency_missing with zero writes; stale, duplicate and fork are distinguished without rebuilding or re-signing the record. For status=erasure_pending, accepted or duplicate is returned only after a durable physical-erasure intent keyed by receiver service, account, triggering record and storage boundary exists. Same Idempotency-Key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: The signed record is the only erasure command. Acceptance is forbidden until the receiver has a durable execution intent; physical completion is established only by a verified ErasureReceiptPackage.

operations.notes: Service-authenticated bounded read of a contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range for freshness and replica gap recovery. The Account Authority returns original signed records in status_seq order and never exposes an account to a service without an existing exact account/principal relationship. Empty, unknown and unauthorized are non-enumerating at the operation boundary.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, or bilateral continuity-checkpoint control. The continuity branch carries a one-sided proposal; the receiver recomputes the exact core, verifies the proposer signature, appends only its own participant service-authority signature, durably commits the complete checkpoint and returns it with a signed control receipt. Exact replay returns the same bytes; same-sequence different-digest forks fail closed. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events.

Authenticated single-hop current state refresh. Source-Service-ID equals exact recipient_account_id.station_id; destination and all selector routing Stations equal the authority. Exact recipient/target current joined membership in the named non-minimal Realm gates disclosure. Unknown, unauthorized, inactive, conflict and expired cases return the same empty outcome. No response signature layer exists: consumers authenticate each returned evidence and check actual message scope. known_agent_state_digests permits transport-only state omission; hydrate before canonical root hashing. known_signer_evidence_refs omits only available verified dependencies. Reuse valid state across messages, authorized devices and reconnects; no per-Signal query.

Authenticated Account-Authority-to-origin-Station current-device and revocation gate. returning_session_grant_issue and human session_grant_refresh bind AcceptedDevicePossessionProof; registration/recovery session_grant_issue uses its separately verified durable evidence and forbids this proof. Under one device lock/serializable transaction the origin reads the durable current accepted-device projection, verifies any required proof with its key, derives authorization Event/generation, evaluates pending/revoked state and persists a signed decision receipt binding proof digest and intent. A lock-external key/status read followed by a second gate transaction is forbidden. expected selectors are required for refresh and may be omitted for both issue action classes. Only allow carries derived selectors and can produce complete human device_binding; authority_mismatch maps to device_unauthorized and every non-allow yields zero grant. Exact replay returns the byte-identical <=30 second receipt.

Service-authenticated terminal erasure-result fanout only; it never requests or triggers deletion. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. The receiver verifies the closed trigger union, receipt, issuer authority, every proof, receipt_digest and exact retained-stub binding before durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. Account erasure requires the account_status_record trigger branch to equal the accepted erasure_pending record; other erasure uses the event branch.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; an explicitly selected finite delayed-execution contract carries its required lease/receipt; ordinary offline chat requires neither. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/join/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbsProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch for the Direct Conversation founding exception of zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4: it carries exactly four ordered EventFederationSubmission items (Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create, founder membership join), the source DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceReceipt and bounded dependencies, and it omits service_binding_ref because the Realm does not yet exist at the receiver. The receiver freshly verifies transport source authority over founder_id, cutover/fence continuity when the receipt came from a pre-migration service, destination binding to the local participant, body closure, recomputed founding_unit_digest and coordinates, and the full direct_conversation_genesis admission before admitting the unit at one atomic boundary. The agent_membership_cascade branch preserves the origin-signed controller terminal Event and Agent transitions and applies the same exact controller pair/generation, pre-state exact-set, signer and atomicity rules as self submission. A missing dependency for either registered unit is a retryable top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes, never a per-item partial and never a permanent rejection.
Federation peer actor/data Event causal frontier probe. It never returns a Realm Seal frontier; use ak.peer.seals.read.frontier.v1.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs/digests in one Realm. It never attaches covering or first-activation Seals; Control-Move effectiveness uses the separate Seal frontier/resolve closure. Ordinary DataEvents are authorized by their signed auth_context.authority_refs and portable signer evidence and never enter Seal.delta. Optional peer history_traversal_access accepts only a pending_archive_replica_digest and authorizes delta Control Moves in that exact target-to-base cut; request replicas never grant it.

Authorized federation peer Event scan with self-equivalent selectors and cursor ordering, but a peer-only closed response that excludes realm_state_snapshot_bootstrap. This is a small-history or operator-triggered best-effort fallback; it does not promise an immutable generation, deterministic long-history completion, or historical completeness.

Bounded exact-scope sibling disclosure for fork-resolution per-peer alignment. Each selector is one exact (actor_id, actor_seq) position plus the accepted ak.fork.resolution Event that adjudicates it; there is no cursor, no range and no actor-wide scan, so the cost is bounded by the request instead of by the actor history length. A disclosed position returns the responder complete canonical sibling set at that position, and an empty set is the positive statement that it holds none. A position no settled non-bottom ak.component.fork_resolution.v1 cell adjudicates, an unauthorized peer, an unknown Realm scope and a local budget all collapse into one indistinguishable undisclosed bucket, so this is not a general history read or an enumeration face. Exhaustiveness is an unsigned claim on the same node-to-node authenticated channel that already carries missing_event_ids on ak.peer.events.read.resolve.v1; the challenger recomputes every returned Event identity, and a contradicting disclosure leaves the peer in peer_stale rather than producing new fork evidence.

Private S2S fanout of one byte-identical request+receipt to a closed exact current joined-member ActorId routing projection service or exact RHRK holder service with intersecting archive tuple. Destination authorization, TTL and bytes are signed; no public Event/DeviceMessage.

Private S2S relay of the immutable source record plus SourceRelayAttestation from the source's authenticated current local Station to request_receipt.release_id. Destination validates the relay service against current source delivery/authority binding and performs the only final T1/release linearization. The two-service cut is not globally atomic; v1 assumes honest services and bounded TTL observation.

Private Station to Station invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.account_id.station_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee_account_id equals invite_address.account_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Atomic cross-Station KeyPackage claim. The destination Station is the sole atomic claim-ledger authority for its KeyPackage inventory. The authenticated source Station first validates the participant request against its exact local account/device/generation durable state; revocation_pending fails before any remote call or inventory disclosure and is exposed only as the existing opaque claim_failed result. Request and response carry no PCR/control-history or separate signer-evidence sidecar. Every claim binds the matching accepted authorization Event id, whose unique producer proof and signer evidence must validate when independently replayed, plus the signed destination claim receipt, exact selectors and KeyPackage signature. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and the canonical request digest.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read, the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target. requester_account_id.station_id equals the authenticated Source-Service-ID and every target account_id.station_id equals the Destination-Service-ID; no client SessionGrant, DPoP or local bearer is ever forwarded and clients never call this surface. The destination completes transport authentication before any target read, then re-derives the declared relationship from its own accepted state: realm_membership requires both parties to be current effective joined members of that exact Realm, while contact reads only the target's own current outbound Contact scope and never requires a shared Realm. Purpose is authorized independently. Absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets collapse into an omitted row or device_result_unavailable, rate limited per requester and per target. Rows carry the origin's own attestation and signer evidence ref; the destination adds no response signature. Request <=64 KiB with 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each; complete response <=512 KiB, no continuation. Cross-Station single-use material remains the MLS KeyPackage claim contract.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Private immutable RHRK archive replica to exact holder_service_id. It binds exact archive bytes, container Event, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis and archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for one epoch. First durable acceptance assigns one archive_sequence per semantic key; changing replicated_at cannot add a row. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted receipt. Archive and replay closure are retained for the Realm recovery-material lifetime; v1 defines no remote GC/renewal.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty frontier, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.

Restricted outcome of exactly one forwarded join application, read by the applicant's own Station before that account is a member. The holder Station verifies service-to-service authentication, that applicant_account_id.station_id equals the Source-Service-ID, that it is the Destination-Service-ID, and that event_id is the exact Event this source forwarded for this applicant. received carries no decision; the other five states carry the durable control_proposal_decision_read_outcome for the same proposal and their proposal_state MUST agree. Unknown Realm, unknown Event, wrong source and an application belonging to another account share one non-enumerating not_found. The read discloses nothing beyond this application and never becomes a general governance, roster or proposal listing surface.

Initial closed join intent or opaque continuation cursor; freeze the unique confirmed Realm head and exact request identity, recheck intent and each object scope disclosure authorization on every page/replay. Typed Seal/Control Move/governance dependency/applicant predecessor pages; full independent replay before authoring. Required but undisclosable private-scope material fails with frontier_unavailable. An invite grants no private Circle read authority. 8 MiB per page, never a total history cap.

Pre-join preview of one directed invite, read by the invitee's own Station from the exact inviter Station named by inviter_account_id.station_id. The caller uses service-to-service authentication and never forwards the invitee's local bearer or session credential; requester_account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and the holder MUST be the Destination-Service-ID. The holder resolves the exact invite in its accepted state, checks the invite binds that complete invitee AccountId, is unexpired and unrevoked, and discloses only what the effective ak.realm.preview_policy permits for the invited audience. join_candidates, source_refs, stale and divergent are Directory-result provenance and MUST be omitted. A valid invite whose policy discloses nothing returns the minimal bound preview; unknown Realm, unknown or mismatched invite, wrong source, revoked or expired credential and an absent preview policy share one non-enumerating not_found under a fixed timing bucket. The outcome is not membership and never carries the invite token back.
Authenticated peer Realm Seal frontier discovery using the same RealmSealFrontierView as self.

Authenticated S2S exact resolve of five registered governance-dependency kinds: AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence, and CollisionVariantRecord. Omitted history_traversal_access normally uses ordinary Realm/federation visibility. Its only pre-visibility exception is exact content-addressed AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence whose branch is Service and signer_id equals the responding service itself, so a first-contact receiver can verify that service's historical producer signature without gaining Principal, AccountDevice, Agent, third-party service, Seal, Control Move, membership, roster, or general dependency visibility. The optional pending_archive_replica branch is the sole retained-cut exception. Member request replicas never authorize traversal. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing selectors are same-shape; complete bounds failure returns no partial items or cursor. Includes content-addressed applet_installation_authority dependencies containing the original accepted registration_event and capability_grant_event; consumers authenticate both Events and derive the historical install target before verifying an Applet admission controller.

Near-current S2S group_security_frontier query only. It binds exact base/target Seal bases with exactly one confirmed head per Realm and the closed selector. A pre-Genesis 0 -> 0 request carries proposed_group_genesis_binding in its digest/cache identity; accepted-state requests forbid it and use the winning immutable Genesis binding. Bulk or old history uses receipt/replica-bound direct Seal traversal through standard Event, Seal and governance-dependency resolve. Exact canonical request bytes are bounded by 8 MiB; the complete response remains independently bounded by 1 MiB.

Exact raw seal_refs OR bounded conclusion_queries, never both. Same existing authorization and retained history access; quorum conclusions follow cbs-profiles section 9. No generic private-scope grant. Unknown, unauthorized and unavailable conclusion queries share missing treatment. Request <=64 KiB; response <=8 MiB.

Optional Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. The source batches original producer-signed encrypted SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and one destination service. The destination independently verifies peer authentication, current joined-member ActorId routing authority, envelope proof, scope, Seal, signal_class, TTL and encrypted payload binding, then performs only local live fanout. The request MUST NOT carry Idempotency-Key; uncertain outcomes use drop_unconfirmed. A successful request returns an empty response; it reveals no Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, support, or per-signal result and is not a durable delivery receipt.

The wrapper carries one DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, did, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and did and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core did refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No did is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with did, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published did and signed receipt, with project(did)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

The configured Account Station provides verified public identity resolution to its clients through this standard operation. Clients bind the exact DID/subject/purpose to their trusted Station context without fetching method history. A server or independent verifier admitting external resolver material validates the native method evidence and historical authority; remote self-assertions are not trusted. Registration before an Account session requires the expected authenticated registration service/issuer binding. Requested evidence must be derived from verified state or fail closed.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventInitialSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control Seal MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before Seal materialization it returns retry-safe frontier_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Creates one durable recovery session owned by the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt presented as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP. request_id, canonical create intent, candidate device, principal, audience and grant coordinates are immutable. Same request identity plus identical intent returns the retained session; a different intent or reuse of one grant for another session fails duplicate_conflict.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Requires the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt frozen by create. Proof transcript binds request_id, grant id, cnf.jkt and the complete recovery session tuple. Exact proof replay returns the retained verified outcome; another proof intent after terminal transition fails closed.

Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) registration key. The client supplies did plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=did, projects did to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact account-local PCR Realm selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Profile writes are ordinary data. Successful durable independent admission returns the outcome without Seal coverage or advancement; exact retry returns the stored byte-identical outcome. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no account-local-lineage selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Bounded account long polling with independently paged Realm summaries, at most 16 selected Realm details, segmented global baselines, explicit filter replacement and durable cursor recovery. Empty Realm selection returns no detail. Current authorization and invalidation channels are never window-filtered. Canonical frame <=8 MiB; a round <=16 MiB and <=16 frames; see client-sync section 2.3. HTTP filter and realm_list each use one percent-encoded RFC 8785 JSON query value, preserving empty objects/arrays; dotted/deepObject aliases are not accepted. notifications.items is one closed union discriminated by id form: ak:notification:<uuidv7> is the Agent runtime approval branch and ak:notification_projection:<token> is the ordinary source-Event current row, sharing one projection position, one notifications baseline channel and the same per-frame budget. Ordinary rows carry no inbox state and are re-authorized on every frame, frozen baseline pages included; there is no second notification list operation. See client-sync section 3.1.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Only outward carrier for the PCR-resident ak.profile.create / ak.profile.update facts. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through a Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector on ak.self.events.read.scan.v1. Authorization is current effective joined membership of body realm_id for both the caller and each returned actor; realm_id MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm. Each row returns the display projection and one exact signed profile Event as provenance. No covering Seal exists for these ordinary writes. The authenticated own-Station projection is not an independently proven complete CRDT state; a patch Event alone cannot reconstruct the full profile. It grants no authority and exposes no other PCR Event. Unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, non-member actor and unauthorized caller all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot probe membership or account existence.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Authenticated controller view. Delegated Account Authority executing pair_agent_key may use authenticated confidential S2S access to this same operation and receive key_state.runtime_verifier_material bound to the exact handle/candidate for independent PoP verification. Ordinary controller/runtime responses MUST omit that field; no generic account impersonation or caller-selected candidate is allowed.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

The active Applet service submits only Realm, exact external tuple, and optional display input.
