The Station derives every current registration, grant, registration-epoch, package, hosting, and time coordinate, atomically supersedes any prior uncommitted generation for the same branch subject, and returns the exact persisted signed authoring request.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Station durably records the current subject generation and exact signed request before returning
No Event is admitted, but the Station atomically persists the branch-subject winner, exact unsigned payload, exact signed request, and superseded generations before returning

operations.notes: Read-only preflight of exactly one non-empty submissions (complete online EventInitialSubmission inputs, with no authorization_lease) or intents array. MLS Genesis/Commit public leaf inputs are independently checked against the signed exact basis. Never admits Events or reserves a frontier. Bare events arrays are forbidden.

Query parameters are realm_id, optional subject_actor_id and optional at. subject_actor_id is a percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId, including Account and Service branches. Omission selects the authenticated credential's exact ActorId. subject_actor_id is the only accepted subject parameter, so subject, subject_station_id and subject_account_id are invalid; no principal-only, local-service, bearer-service, DID-document or inferred-routing fallback is allowed.

Optional query realm_id and cursor. Explicit subject and subject_station_id MUST be paired did_core_id values identifying an exact AccountId. Omitting both selects only the authenticated credential's exact AccountId. Handles, principal-only requests and inferred Station fallbacks are forbidden; self authorization compares the entire AccountId.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through ordinary Event admission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_id, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id and the complete target ActorId is payload.member_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission. Path actor_id is one percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId segment, not a bare principal DID; it is a route selector and does not rename the Event field. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed head_eq guard; payload.circle_id MUST equal its path identifier and payload.member_id MUST equal the entire decoded path ActorId, including Station and branch. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move carried in grant_event through ordinary Event admission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated cell subject and the security-set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (the exact current authority-root controller; root_control_only forbids independent controller/Agent delegation).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell. On admission the recipient Station writes one holder-private ak.account.holder_quarantine entry with surface_kind consent_request, carrying no Event ref and none of the invite_delivery branch members; it shares the invite delivery quota, ledger and CAS chokepoint. Because this operation declares no idempotency key and carries no nonce, that branch deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness over (account_id, source_peer_principal_id, consent_scope). The written entry is holder-private service-local material, so durable_effect stays none.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move carried in revoke_event through ordinary Event admission. Its payload.observed_dot_ids MUST enumerate the active grant dots being removed for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope), read back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots. Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes and MUST still enumerate every dot; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell selected by the required peer query parameter. The authenticated actor determines the holder coordinate; peers never receive this DTO.

Holder-authorized deterministic compaction of the oldest contiguous terminal Contact prefix. The server computes the core from accepted history; callers cannot submit or choose it. Cross-service pairs use the continuity_checkpoint branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1: the receiver recomputes, countersigns, durably commits and returns the complete checkpoint in one round trip, then the proposer commits the exact returned bytes. Exact replay returns the same checkpoint; same sequence with another digest is continuity_invalid and has no winner. Export reuses continuity_evidence on ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 and import reuses the Contact request continuity_evidence field.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. The same trust domain and exact ActorId pair cannot reset its lineage or founding slot. Missing continuity must be recovered or explicitly imported; a full tail without a bilateral checkpoint stays blocked. Only an explicitly initiated first contact for a legally different exact ActorId pair creates an independent root, without inherited checkpoint, history, audit identity, DM or MLS state.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1 operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Authenticated holder projection from server-verified durable Contact evidence. pending_incoming includes request_event_ref and the exact optional request_message; respond/reject use peer and request_event_ref. Complete continuity_evidence is exported only for explicit boolean query include_continuity=true (default false); online recontact uses Station durable checkpoint and bounded tail. Private Consent and account-data notes are not Contact authority.

Issue one immutable current-authority authority Ack for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct authority Acks and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Authenticated submission of one complete signed_defer or signed_reject. The receiver loads the durable accepted proposal and its immutable canonical ControlProposalAck, recomputes proposal_ack_digest, verifies the exact Realm/proposal/authority-set/deadline/defer chain and quorum, then atomically persists the decision. Exact decision replay is byte-identical duplicate; conflicting terminal or post-Seal decisions fail closed. For ak.device.revoke, only a valid signed_reject for the exact proposal/Ack (therefore the exact reducer-derived device and generation) clears that proposal's revocation_pending record; it clears no other pending revoke for the device.

Authenticated exact proposal observation surface. Returns only the durable authority discriminator, canonical Ack when applicable, verified decision chain and covering Seal state for the requested Realm/proposal digest. control_proposal_ack permits the closed pending/deferred/overdue/rejected/sealed chain and always carries Ack; the narrow ackless_event_proof branch permits only pending/sealed and carries no Ack, decision or Ack-derived deadline fault. ak.device.revoke is always control_proposal_ack. The operation cannot mint an Ack, synthesize a reject or mutate pending state; unauthorized and unknown selectors are non-enumerating.

Authenticated exact AccountId selects its unique accepted PCR and current PrincipalResolutionProjection, independent of optional profile. Before the first accepted Seal, only the exact atomically accepted genesis current is eligible while no accepted resolution successor exists; derived cache metadata is not authority. The own Station validates method history; no portable evidence or observation time is returned. Wrong or invisible account returns not_found; unresolved verified current state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_account_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists. Found MUST include coordinates.binding_event_ref naming an accepted endorsement for authoring. Clients trust their own Station current result and exact sealed proposal decision; they do not replay a governance history closure.

A single ordinary Event may authenticate itself using ProofAuthenticatedPublication at any eligible receiver, retaining its full original ActorId/AccountId. No SessionGrant, origin handoff, origin device-check callback or fresh authority lease is required for that branch. Security, batch, private and atomic bootstrap requests keep their registered authentication requirements. Initial durable Event publication uses EventInitialSubmission: the signed Event remains the only business fact, while AuthorizationLease and optional CbsProofBundle values are independently verified publication evidence outside the Event digest. Before live acceptance, each receiving Station checks all locally known exact device revocation fences in the same durable admission transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and zero Event/proof writes. Accepted ak.device.revoke is Ack-required and atomically writes its derived exact device/generation pending record. For a locally authored Realm Event, canonical acceptance, the complete distinct recipient-service target set and every target outbox intent commit atomically. A missing route creates durable pending_route and never rejects the Event; each send rechecks the frozen exact joined-member ActorId routing authority, authority loss terminally cancels the old target, and submit exposes only pending_delivery_count; clients derive delivery state as pending iff the count is non-zero. The ingress MUST persist and return the original IngressReceipt before lease expiry; byte-identical retry returns the stored receipt without changing received_at. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer remains the authoritative state machine and re-checks token commitment, allowlist, replay, proposal and expiry state. The direct_conversation_founding branch remains its closed four-Event atomic unit: Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create and founder membership join. The agent_membership_cascade branch is the only controller-cascade carrier: atomic_self_leave accepts the controller terminal Event and the exact pre-state Agent leave set all-or-nothing; emergency_terminal accepts a third-party terminal Event and atomically freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent without synthesizing Agent Events; emergency_cleanup accepts only the same initiator's complete signed Agent leave set and commits it atomically. Effective Agent membership is invalid immediately after the terminal transition, independent of cleanup completion. Exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome, while the same cleanup intent with different canonical content is duplicate_conflict.

Return the complete durable frozen fanout target set for one caller-visible accepted Event. Unknown and invisible Events share not_found. Rows use stable opaque target_id and are sorted byte-wise; service_id is included only when the caller can currently read an exact contributing joined-member ActorId routing projection. The query has no retry, route-resolution or delivery side effect.
Actor/data Event causal frontier only. actor_id is required; Realm Seal discovery is exclusively ak.self.seals.read.frontier.v1.

Dereference exact event_id/event_digest selectors. Optional self history_traversal_access authorizes only delta Control Moves in one retained target-to-base direct traversal cut and is mutually exclusive with ordinary timeline visibility. Point lookup is not a range scan and never attaches covering/first-activation Seals; Control-Move effectiveness uses Seal frontier/resolve.
Canonical safe and idempotent Events range scan. HTTP uses RFC 10008 QUERY with typed JSON content.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Own-Station signing input for a Realm genesis the authenticated caller is about to author. The exact session account and its serving Station select the accepted deployment notary configuration for the requested collaboration or direct_conversation purpose; the Station names its own Seal verification_method and the caller copies the value verbatim without constructing a fragment or fetching method history. Success creates no Realm, reserves no identifier and grants no authoring authority. Wrong or invisible account returns not_found; no verified configuration yet returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Create one immutable scope-private history request. The operation envelope may be at most 1 MiB, while the inner HistoryKeyRequest itself is independently capped at 64 KiB canonical bytes. Before success the service verifies the caller-pinned bootstrap/current bases and complete durable target cut, atomically pins every Seal, delta Control Move and registered dependency through request expiry, freezes the exact direct traversal intent, durably stores request/receipt bytes, generates a 32-byte CSPRNG response capability and returns its byte-stable HPKE-sealed carrier. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted outcome; different intent under the same request_id conflicts.

List immutable current-member-only requests for the exact Realm/Circle scope. realm_id is required; circle_id absence selects Realm scope. The RHRK-holder branch returns only requests whose ranges intersect an archive sealed to the caller's exact historical key.

Capability-protected contiguous high-water ack. Every covered sequence requires a durable installed, cryptographically_rejected, superseded_duplicate or signed service_record_lost disposition. Manifest installed means descriptor installation only; no reject/lost/manifest disposition completes epoch coverage.

Durably enqueue one immutable manifest or independently sealed chunk. Manifest admission first resolves and replays the receipt-retained direct Seal/Event/dependency cut, derives current requester incarnation, join floor, winning MLS transitions and current monotone history_access, and atomically writes the all-ranges admission or nothing. A chunk requires that accepted admission, then enforces current T1 and writes the recipient record plus attestation. Premature/mismatched chunks are dependency_missing with zero pending state. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical small accepted HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt.

Capability-bound stream from the Account Station frozen by the accepted request. Complete sequence-prefix page <=8 MiB includes deduplicated historical source signer results and exact group ciphersuite. Client verifies source signatures and end-to-end bindings, never governance history. Cursor/ACK cannot cross an unresolved reserved slot.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted Seal covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact account_id; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. account_id is server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Station. invite_event_id must resolve to an Event already accepted by this service and authored by the current session actor. The service reads its own stored canonical Event bytes; local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path and remote delivery builds the peer request from those bytes.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage and mls_history series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.
Issue a durable current-device-only challenge with lifetime at most 300 seconds. Recovery unlock reuses its recovery session challenge.
Same still-authorized holder exact replay returns the durable unlock outcome without charging the one-use challenge again.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the same empty success response, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Station's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Station verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current joined-member ActorId routing projection; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Authenticated cross-account device directory and published prekey-bundle read. Selectors are bounded at 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each with a 64 KiB canonical request; an over-limit request fails whole. Disclosure requires a current authorization relationship - a Realm the requester still joins, or a current Contact/call/session context, where the Contact case never requires a shared Realm. Targets hosted by another Station are resolved through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 and verified locally before the row is returned; the client never contacts a foreign Station and its session credential is never forwarded. failures[].reason_code is the closed pair device_result_unavailable and device_directory_unavailable, and an unavailable fetch is never rendered as an empty device set.

Own-Station verified route and signing keys for the media service anchored by one joined Realm current accepted ak.component.realm.media_service.v1 cell. Membership visibility and the anchored cell are evaluated under one confirmed basis with exactly one head per Realm; the caller supplies no service id, DID, base URL or candidate origin. The result resolves service identity, purpose and route only: it releases no media key, no backend token and no plaintext-visibility authorization, and expires_at bounds route and key reuse to at most 300 seconds. Invisible Realm or absent anchor returns not_found; unresolved accepted state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and complete response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Prepare one complete unsigned ak.message.create from a closed intent, after client encryption where required. Exact canonical request replay; expires at client created_at plus 300 seconds. No sequence reservation and no submit ticket.

durable_effect.rationale: Only a bounded expiring preparation cache; no accepted Event, sequence, membership or projection mutation.

operations.notes: Carries exactly one direct-holder signed report_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned report fields. The Event kind is ak.self.moderation.report; this self endpoint accepts only absent/self provenance and forbids source_provider_id, delegated executor, Applet and MIMI-facade provenance. event.actor_id and payload.reporter must equal the authenticated session principal. There is no path Realm: event.realm_id, payload.realm_id, signed scope_ref and the accepted target's derived governance scope must match exactly. Realm-default reports may omit payload.effective_scope; Circle reports must sign the exact Circle scope. The target must be accepted and visible to the reporter; absent, invisible and scope-mismatched targets use the same not_found response. This DataEvent carries auth_context.authority_refs and no seal_ref and cannot carry seal_basis or preconditions. The service forwards exact signed bytes through ordinary Event admission and never authors, rebuilds, co-signs, maps an operation ref to another target or adds a concurrency guard. report_id is derived by retyping the accepted Event id and the stored submit outcome has status=submitted. Exact replay returns that byte-identical outcome without a second log or queue append; the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict. routed_to is omitted for an ordinary reporter and may be returned only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the exact scope.

Optional authenticated time-existence evidence for the exact ordinary franking-proof Event, its target and service key validity interval. Return one confirmed security Seal containing the exact existence_anchor plus the necessary ordinary Event ancestry. The proof Event never enters Seal.delta or a data observation root, and ordinary chat never waits for this evidence.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Recipient-bound byte-paged archive list. Query and cursor bind scope/key tuple, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis, holder authority and last ordering tuple. Every row carries the exact holder-accepted archive_replica_digest plus archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for its singleton epoch. The holder MUST use that digest as the closed SelfHistoryTraversalAccess coordinate and may resolve every Control Move/Seal/dependency required by that replay, including membership/policy/control metadata; archive/traversal digests, unrelated DataEvents and generic timeline scan are forbidden substitutes. Unknown/unauthorized/tuple mismatch is same-shape not_found.

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or co-sign. The cursor object carries neither an id nor an updated_at — a cursor is never updated in place, its identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple and there is no read_cursor typed ID kind — so the update time of an advance is the Event envelope created_at, and the read_marker_outcome updated_at is that derived envelope time of the winning advance. Sibling devices observe the winner as the ak.read_cursor.update device message whose content is ak.schema.read_cursor_update.v1. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Prepare exactly one Realm join, knock or invite acceptance. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. The Station resolves the canonical Realm, runs the bounded first-contact bootstrap when it holds no accepted state for that Realm, independently verifies the returned facts against their dependency closure, and freezes the effective join_rule, complete accepted seal_basis, live digest suite, encryption profile, the exact Event kind, canonical payload and preconditions. The client checks target, purpose, request binding and the exact bytes, then signs and submits through ak.self.events.command.submit.v1; it never fetches remote governance evidence, never recomputes Seal roots, never selects a candidate endpoint and never runs a reducer. Preparation is not admission: submit re-checks current authority, freshness and basis, and a stale or conflicting basis requires a fresh preparation instead of rewriting signed material. Registered intents are invite_accept, member_join and knock; restricted_join and application receipts are unsupported_feature. The actor frontier is derived separately from the governance basis under event-and-patch section 2.6, over the union of locally verified accepted state, the applicant's own verified history and the independently verified bootstrap predecessors; remote material never lowers or overrides local history. next_actor_seq zero requires all four decidable initial-state conditions: this service is the account's own Station and therefore the sole authoring entry, the durable authoring record is unbroken since inception across the current device generation lineage, enumeration of that realm and actor completed deterministically and empty, and the verified bootstrap predecessors are empty. Otherwise the operation fails with frontier_unavailable and is recovered through ordinary authorized sync, bootstrap, actor chain repair or fork resolution, never by rejoining to reset the chain.

Own-Station validated progress of one join application authored by this account before membership exists. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. origin_state reports this Station's own durable forwarding fact and is never Realm acceptance; realm_state appears only after a bounded candidate answered, and accepted_seal_id appears only when this Station has itself verified and accepted the covering Seal. The outcome carries no Ack, authority set, authority signature or Seal bytes: after sealed the account is a member and continues through the ordinary member federation and sync surfaces. Unknown Event, another account's application and a non-matching session share one non-enumerating not_found.

Own-Station validated pre-join Realm preview. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. The invite target is resolved only against inviter_account_id.station_id, taking the equivalent local path when that Station is this service; every other target is resolved through the Directory discovery input surface and independently validated before it becomes a result. The client never calls the source, never selects a forwarding candidate and never goes back to a truth source: join_candidates, source_refs, stale and divergent are omitted. request_digest binds the exact chosen target, and source names where the disclosure came from. An unreachable source is a retryable upstream failure and MUST NOT be replaced by another service identity or another Realm member Station.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

Registered repair-material read for one Relation primary conflict domain. The Station returns the frozen baseline (complete member_count plus the chained members_digest) and exactly one 256-member page of the canonically ordered candidate list; a page never takes effect alone, and the client walks every page in ascending page_index over the prev_page_digest chain before signing an ak.relation.resolve against that members_digest. The ordinary 16-head diagnostic bound governs only the optional diagnostic field and MUST NOT truncate, reorder or refuse this material: a group that already failed with relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded is exactly the group that needs it. The caller must be authorized to read every candidate in the group; a partially visible group returns relation_conflict_group_not_visible rather than a shortened list, and retained-but-unreadable material returns relation_conflict_material_unavailable instead of a truncated page. A chain break, gap, reorder or mid-read group change returns relation_conflict_material_page_gap and the read restarts at page_index=0.

Prepare only an f=0 device-signed human/Agent PCR successor Seal. The authenticated Account Station validates the exact confirmed predecessor, configuration, ordered command outcomes, full final effects and availability dependencies. It durably freezes the complete canonical request, body and view=0 before responding. Client compares Realm, predecessor, configuration, requested execution order and HLC, then signs the canonical ak.seal.commit.v1 transcript, not raw body bytes. Exact retry returns the identical result. Timeout, cache eviction and restart do not release the fence; only a confirmed successor or legal configuration handoff advances it. This operation is not multi-replica prepare/view-change transport. Ordinary data needs no prepare. Digest transitions and compaction use their registered paths.

Submit a complete Seal and its commit quorum certificate directly. Recompute stable body identity, single predecessor continuity, ordered command results, registered effects, safety roots, configuration and ak.seal.commit.v1 signatures. Ordinary data cannot enter the safety delta.
Realm Seal frontier discovery. Returns the complete canonical accepted Seal basis with exactly one confirmed head per Realm, governance health and observation coordinate.

Resolve a caller-split batch of five typed dependency kinds: the content-addressed AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence and MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence, plus CollisionVariantRecord selected by collision_variant_record_id and verified against the referencing ak.fork.resolution locator digest. Optional self history_traversal_access is the sole retained-cut visibility exception. The operation is cursor-free and returns no partial result when the complete same-shape outcome exceeds byte_limit or 8 MiB. Includes content-addressed applet_installation_authority dependencies containing the original accepted registration_event and capability_grant_event; consumers authenticate both Events and derive the historical install target before verifying an Applet admission controller.
Current exact membership, MLS join epoch and scope policy floor. Request and complete response each at most 64 KiB. No client governance checkpoint or replay; not a key release grant.

Current accepted membership incarnation for one exact Realm/Circle and ActorId at the current confirmed basis. Recheck current requester visibility and target membership; no client replay, all-members list or history closure. Request and complete response each at most 64 KiB.

One known Genesis/Commit/Welcome on the current accepted winning transition chain. Recheck current requester/scope and artifact visibility, including Welcome recipient binding. Return the exact admitted transition leaf input and binding, with no client governance replay. Request at most 64 KiB; complete response at most 16 MiB.

Authenticated Account Station group security-frontier result at exact seal_basis and caller-local MLS leaves. No proof_base_basis, Merkle witness, history closure or client replay. The result binds the request digest, governance binding and exact accepted epoch CAS head. Peer proof verification remains independent. Exact canonical request bytes are bounded by 8 MiB; the complete response remains independently bounded by 1 MiB.

Own-Station exact current MLS base-tree reconciliation. Current authorization and per-leaf retained admission incarnation/key binding determine a complete sorted removal subset; no client governance history. Request <=8 MiB, complete response <=1 MiB; no continuation.

Authenticated exact recipient Welcome reference discovery in one Realm/Circle and MLS group. Current authorization on every frozen-window page; 20 default, 100 maximum references; request and complete response each at most 64 KiB. No artifact bytes, governance proof, consume or notification ACK.

Own/delegated PCR-only bounded discovery from the durable pending index. Exact current accepted predecessor basis and current device/controller authorization required. Returns at most limit pending digests plus has_more; no complete history, cursor, ACK, or implicit admission. Re-read after a sealed batch. Exact Event acceptance remains the control-proposal decision result.

Exact raw seal_refs OR bounded conclusion_queries, never both. Same existing authorization and retained history access; quorum conclusions follow cbs-profiles section 9. No generic private-scope grant. Unknown, unauthorized and unavailable conclusion queries share missing treatment. Request <=64 KiB; response <=8 MiB.

Continues only the next step derived from the transaction kind and accepted-step prefix length. request_digest and prepared_plan_digest MUST equal the resource, while expected_accepted_step_count MUST equal the current prefix length; the endpoint is not a generic step or Saga executor. Client attestation is required only for issue_terminal_receipt or local_commit and must bind transaction/request/plan plus the pre-reserved output_ref. When all coordinator-owned steps are accepted but the device is offline, terminal_result remains absent; device-attestation readiness is a computed view of the canonical next step and no coordinator phase/state is serialized.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.

Encrypted-only Signal Extension send rail for ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. Exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. It MUST NOT persist the envelope as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.

Own Station validates 1..64 exact account-device/Agent current or historical selectors. Current keys serve this validation invocation only. Historical receiver is this authenticated recipient Station and the Event must be locally accepted and readable; Device and Agent history independently resolve the original producer key from portable immutable authorization evidence and apply known closure decisions. Request <=64 KiB; each result <=16 KiB; complete response <=1 MiB. Exactly one resolved/unavailable result per selector; no portable closure, caller-selected receiver, or current-directory substitution for history.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Purpose-scoped acceptance attestation the authenticated inviter obtains from its own Station for one exact ak.invite.third_party it authored (third-party-invites.md section 7.4). The Station evaluates its current accepted basis, confirms the caller authored the invite, that the invite cell is pending, and that verification_id matches the cell and the current allowlist, then signs an attestation binding station_id, verification_id, audience, realm_id, invite_id, inviter_account_id, provisioning_id, the exact public material, invite_expires_at, invite_state, accepted_seal_id, observed_at and its own expires_at. The caller supplies no governance material and receives no governance closure, Seal ancestry or membership listing; the attestation authorizes nothing except activation of the named provisioning record. Not visible, not authored by the caller and not pending all return the uniform section 6 not_found; a basis the Station cannot currently confirm returns frontier_unavailable.
